title: Mutual NDA playbook, discloser-weighted (Corvel Robotics, Party 1)
provenance: Draft, 15 October 2026 (BENCHMARK-V2.md P1), for layer A v2: the discloser-weighted position set over the 17 rule ids of the ContractNLI NDA playbook (contractnli/playbook-nda.json, whose balanced positions are unchanged). Our standard terms are the Common Paper Mutual NDA Version 1.0 with the cover terms of v2/base-nda.json, so the clean copy meets every preferred position; the two NDA position sets differ in which direction of change is a departure and how far each side will go. Each rule's source records the Common Paper text or annotation it rests on. Written by us with Claude Opus 5.5 (disclosed); fictional parties; not legal advice; not lawyer validated; not frozen until the ambiguity read (P2) and calibration (P8).

rules.title: How confidential information is identified
rules.guidance: We disclose designs, roadmaps and pricing in meetings and demonstrations as well as in documents, so protection must not depend on marking. The two-limb test of the Standard Terms is our standard.
rules.preferred: Information is Confidential Information if the Disclosing Party identifies it as confidential or proprietary, or if it should reasonably be understood as confidential from its nature and the circumstances of disclosure.
rules.acceptable: Marking or written identification required for documents, provided the reasonable-understanding limb still applies to everything else.
rules.escalation: Protection limited to information marked or expressly identified as confidential, with no reasonable-understanding limb.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 (two limbs: identified as confidential, or reasonably understood as confidential). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "some companies require marking", with a suggested edit removing the "reasonably understood" prong; the page also notes the definition does not reach information disclosed before the Effective Date and offers an edit extending it.

rules.title: Scope of confidential information
rules.guidance: The definition must reach every category we will share: product designs, roadmap, pricing and security documentation, technical and business information alike.
rules.preferred: A definition that includes technical and business information, product designs or roadmaps, requirements, pricing, security and compliance documentation, technology, inventions and know-how.
rules.acceptable: A shorter list of examples, provided business information (including pricing and roadmaps) and technical information both stay within the definition.
rules.escalation: Any category we disclose (product designs, roadmaps, pricing or security documentation) excluded or narrowed out of the definition, or the definition limited to technical information.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 list (technical or business information, product designs or roadmaps, requirements, pricing, security and compliance documentation, technology, inventions and know-how). The page gives "vendor security documentation" as an example of what an NDA protects.

rules.title: Oral and visual disclosures
rules.guidance: Much of what we share is shown in demonstrations, site visits and calls. It must be protected on the same footing as documents.
rules.preferred: Information is protected in whatever form it is disclosed or made available, including orally, visually or by demonstration.
rules.acceptable: Oral and visual disclosures protected if identified as confidential when made or confirmed in writing within 30 days.
rules.escalation: Oral, visual or demonstrated information excluded from protection, or protected only if confirmed in writing within fewer than 30 days.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1 protects information the Disclosing Party may "disclose or make available", without limiting its form; no annotation on the page addresses oral disclosure.

rules.title: Use limited to the purpose
rules.guidance: The other party may use what we share only to evaluate the deal described in the Purpose.
rules.preferred: Use solely for the Purpose on the Cover Page, which is limited to evaluating the business relationship it describes.
rules.acceptable: Use for the Purpose and for internal evaluation directly connected with it.
rules.escalation: Any wider use: a Purpose extended beyond evaluating the relationship (for example to developing, improving or marketing the Receiving Party's own products), a residuals clause, or use for anything not expressly prohibited.
rules.hardLine: A right to use Confidential Information for any purpose.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(a). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "The Purpose limits how Confidential Information may be used", with examples from broad evaluation of a business relationship to narrow reviews of vendor security documentation. A residuals clause appears only as a Language Library option, without commentary.

rules.title: Sharing with employees
rules.guidance: Employees of the other party may see our information only when they need it for the Purpose and are bound to keep it confidential, and the other party answers for them.
rules.preferred: Disclosure to employees with a reasonable need to know for the Purpose, bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than the MNDA, the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance.
rules.acceptable: The same, limited to named employees or employees who have signed an acknowledgement.
rules.escalation: Disclosure to employees without a need to know, without being bound by confidentiality obligations, or without the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(b): employees and other representatives with a reasonable need to know, bound by obligations no less protective, the Receiving Party remaining responsible. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Sharing with advisers and other representatives
rules.guidance: Advisers, contractors and other representatives may see our information on the same terms as employees. Affiliates under common control may be added on those terms.
rules.preferred: Disclosure to agents, advisors, contractors and other representatives with a reasonable need to know, bound by obligations no less protective than the MNDA, the Receiving Party remaining responsible for their compliance; no disclosure to affiliates.
rules.acceptable: Affiliates under common control added as permitted recipients on the same need-to-know, bound and responsible terms.
rules.escalation: Disclosure to any third party (including affiliates, contractors or advisers) without a need to know, without being bound by equivalent obligations, or without the Receiving Party remaining responsible for them; or third-party disclosure deemed approved.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 2(b). Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): section 2 "does not extend to sister entities or affiliates"; the page suggests an edit adding affiliates under common control.

rules.title: Compelled disclosure
rules.guidance: If the other party is compelled by law to disclose our information, we need warning so we can seek protection, and nothing beyond what the law requires should go out.
rules.preferred: Disclosure only to the extent required by law, regulation, subpoena or court order, with reasonable advance notice (where legally permitted) and reasonable cooperation, at our expense, with our efforts to obtain confidential treatment.
rules.acceptable: Notice as soon as practicable where advance notice is not possible, or no obligation to cooperate.
rules.escalation: Compelled disclosure with no notice where notice is lawful, disclosure beyond what is legally required, or the exception widened to requests that are not legally binding (for example informal regulator, auditor or customer requests).
rules.source: Standard Terms section 4 (reasonable advance notice to the extent legally permitted; reasonable cooperation at the Disclosing Party's expense). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Confidentiality of the agreement and discussions
rules.guidance: That we are talking to this counterparty, and on what terms, is itself confidential.
rules.preferred: The existence and status of the discussions and the information on the Cover Page are Confidential Information of each party.
rules.acceptable: Disclosure of the existence of the MNDA (but not the subject of the discussions) to professional advisers, financiers or as required by law.
rules.escalation: The discussions or the Cover Page information removed from Confidential Information, or a right for either party to announce or publicise the discussions without consent.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 1: "Each party's Confidential Information also includes the existence and status of the parties' discussions and information on the Cover Page." No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Reverse engineering
rules.guidance: Use is already limited to the Purpose and no licence is granted, so silence on reverse engineering is our standard. An express prohibition is welcome; an express right to analyse our materials is not.
rules.preferred: The MNDA is silent on reverse engineering.
rules.acceptable: An express mutual prohibition on reverse engineering, decompiling or disassembling materials provided under the MNDA.
rules.escalation: An express right to reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, analyse or test samples, prototypes or software we provide, or a statement that doing so is not a use of Confidential Information.
rules.source: The Standard Terms say nothing on reverse engineering; use is limited to the Purpose (section 2(a)) and no licence is granted (section 7). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Independent development
rules.guidance: The independent-development exception is standard, but the other party must show the development did not use or reference our information.
rules.preferred: Information the Receiving Party can demonstrate it independently developed without using or referencing the Confidential Information is excluded.
rules.acceptable: The same exclusion, demonstrated by contemporaneous written records.
rules.escalation: The exclusion widened beyond development without use or reference (for example development by personnel who had access, development "without intentional use", or use of information retained in memory), or the Receiving Party's burden to demonstrate it removed.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 3(d), with the Receiving Party bearing the burden ("information that it can demonstrate"). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Information from third parties
rules.guidance: Information the other party rightfully gets from someone free to share it is excluded, but only then.
rules.preferred: Information the Receiving Party can demonstrate it rightfully obtained from a third party without confidentiality restrictions is excluded.
rules.acceptable: The same, with the third party's freedom from restriction judged on the Receiving Party's reasonable knowledge.
rules.escalation: Information from a third party excluded whether or not obtained rightfully or free of confidentiality restrictions, or the Receiving Party's burden to demonstrate it removed.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 3(c), with the same burden. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: No licence or transfer of rights
rules.guidance: Sharing grants no rights. Our designs and roadmap stay ours.
rules.preferred: The Disclosing Party retains all intellectual property and other rights in its Confidential Information, and disclosure grants no licence.
rules.acceptable: A licence limited to using Confidential Information for the Purpose during the MNDA Term.
rules.escalation: Any licence or right beyond use for the Purpose, any transfer of rights in Confidential Information, or removal of the retention-of-rights statement.
rules.hardLine: An assignment of the Disclosing Party's intellectual property.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 7. The page annotates section 8 (Disclaimer): the NDA "is meant for preliminary discussions, not product use".

rules.title: Return or destruction
rules.guidance: When the MNDA ends, or earlier when we ask, the other party stops using our information and returns or destroys it, and confirms that on request.
rules.preferred: On expiry, termination or our earlier request the Receiving Party ceases use; promptly after our written request it destroys or returns all Confidential Information; it confirms compliance in writing if requested.
rules.acceptable: Return or destruction within 30 days after the request, at the Receiving Party's choice, with written confirmation on request.
rules.escalation: No obligation to cease use, or to return or destroy on request; a period longer than 30 days; or no written confirmation when requested.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 6(a) to (c) (cease use; return or destroy promptly after written request; confirm in writing if requested). No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Copies
rules.guidance: Copies of our information are our information. Silence is our standard; reasonable working copies under the same obligations are fine.
rules.preferred: The MNDA is silent on copies, so every copy is Confidential Information under the same obligations.
rules.acceptable: Copies permitted as reasonably necessary for the Purpose, carrying the same markings and obligations.
rules.escalation: A right to make copies free of the MNDA's obligations, or copies for anything other than the Purpose.
rules.source: The Standard Terms say nothing on copies; a copy of Confidential Information is itself Confidential Information under sections 1, 2 and 6. No annotation on the page.

rules.title: Non-solicitation
rules.guidance: A confidentiality agreement should not carry restrictive covenants; a non-solicitation belongs in a separate agreement, if anywhere.
rules.preferred: No non-solicitation, no-hire, non-compete or exclusivity provision.
rules.acceptable: A mutual non-solicitation of employees met through the discussions, for no more than 12 months, excluding general advertising.
rules.escalation: A one-sided non-solicitation, any no-hire, a restriction longer than 12 months, or one covering employees not met through the discussions.
rules.hardLine: A non-compete or exclusivity obligation binding either party.
rules.source: The Standard Terms have no restrictive covenant and say "Neither party has an obligation under this MNDA to ... proceed with any proposed transaction" (section 11); the page does not mention non-solicitation.

rules.title: Survival of obligations
rules.guidance: Our roadmap and pricing stay sensitive after the evaluation ends. Protection must outlast the MNDA Term, and trade secrets must be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.
rules.preferred: A Term of Confidentiality of 2 years from the Effective Date (with a 1-year MNDA Term), trade secrets protected until they are no longer trade secrets, and early termination not shortening it.
rules.acceptable: A fixed Term of Confidentiality of at least 18 months from the Effective Date, or protection in perpetuity, with trade secrets protected while they remain trade secrets.
rules.escalation: A Term of Confidentiality shorter than 18 months from the Effective Date, one that ends when the MNDA expires or is terminated, or removal of the trade-secret extension.
rules.source: Cover Page Term of Confidentiality and Standard Terms section 5. Common Paper Mutual NDA page (https://commonpaper.com/standards/mutual-nda/, read 15 October 2026): "Early termination of the NDA does not shorten the Term of Confidentiality"; 74% use a fixed period, most commonly 2 years, and 26% perpetual; trade secrets protected until they stop being trade secrets; the Cover Page offers the period from the Effective Date or from the date of last disclosure. Common Paper 2026 SaaS contract benchmark report: confidentiality period fixed in 79%, two years in 75% of fixed periods.

rules.title: Retention after return or destruction
rules.guidance: The other party may keep copies only in backups, under its record-retention policies or where the law requires, and the MNDA keeps applying to them.
rules.preferred: Retention only under standard backup or record-retention policies or as required by law, with the MNDA continuing to apply to what is retained.
rules.acceptable: Retention limited to one archival copy kept by legal counsel for compliance, the MNDA continuing to apply.
rules.escalation: Retention for any other purpose, or retained information released from the MNDA's obligations.
rules.source: Standard Terms section 6, last sentence (retention under standard backup or record-retention policies or as required by law, the MNDA continuing to apply). No annotation on the page.
